THE SHAPE CANNOT SILENTLY REGRESS because the premise is DERIVED per call from the same inputs the function already walks: there is no parameter, no flag and no comment asserting it, so nothing is left that can go stale when the anchor moves again. A boolean parameter would have relocated the defect to the caller — a true statement left standing while its premise moved beneath it, which is exactly what happened here.

Probed on both trees in both anchor cases, the field site returns the identical ceiling before and after, while a promise of five with a non-racer anchor moves 1.4400 to 1.1520.

THE PRICE, ten tracks at N=30 and four at N=300, arms matched frame by frame. FRAME COUNTS ARE IDENTICAL BETWEEN ARMS ON ALL TEN TRACKS: this moves the picture and not the race. In-shot p50 is unchanged everywhere and p10 rises by one on the three worst tracks, which is the correct shape: it bites only where the promise was being broken. STEADINESS IS NOT COSTED — largest single-frame pan identical on 9 of 10 at N=30 and on all four at N=300, corner overflow unchanged or better, centreline share unchanged or better. The shot is UNTOUCHED on 82.5-98.7% of frames and where it widens it is a median 1.02-1.07x.

WHAT REMAINS, REPORTED AND NOT CLAMPED. On the frames still short at N=300 the COMPANY ceiling is itself the binding term on 77-100%, with a deficit of exactly one on 85-99%: the guarantee asking and not getting. That is consistent with the recorded defect that the anchor misses the screen point every guarantee reasons from by a median 74 px, and NOT with the headcount still being wrong. No setting was changed to absorb it.
